utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-01-48-T, the Prosecutor versus Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could you make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper Madam Usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Well, just for the issue of all the parties that this afternoon we'll sit from 3.30 until 5.00, instead of 7.00. Yes, Ms. Chana, are you ready were your direct examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Examined by Ms. Chana:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll get the usher to show you a piece of paper. Is your date -- your name and your date of birth reflected on that paper and would you please confirm that these are your details?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes, the details are correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, one minute. I don't seem to be getting the translation. I don't know what the problem is, if you would give me a moment please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: This doesn't look like it's working, Your Honour. Would the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe you could repeat your question to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Pardon, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe you could repeat your question to this witness as a test.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once again, Witness, I think there was a technical hitch. I think it's working now. Could you look at that paper and confirm to this Court, would you, that that's your name and date of birth written on that piece of paper.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes, the details are correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to admit that into evidence

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Obliged, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P337 under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Chana.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: If you go through the background information of this witness, I believe the best way is for us to go to the private session for a short while.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I just realised that. I'm not going to touch on his background anymore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think we should go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, can we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I was asking you what was the composition of the Prozor Independent Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: The Prozor Independent Battalion for the most part comprised Bosniaks from the areas covered by the three towns and villages. Further, it also included Bosniaks who had fled from what we used to refer to at the time as the temporarily occupied territories of the Prozor municipality, mostly Bosniak Muslims. Sometimes persons from some other group would be included. There was, for example, a Bulgarian volunteer. I'm not sure how he came to be in the area; he just appeared there one day. But it was mostly made up of Bosniak persons from the area of Prozor municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you specify which particular places would they come from, these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Those were soldiers from the following villages: Here, Kute, Scipe, Skrobucani, Donja Vast, Klek, Lapsanj, Prozor town, those places mainly. The first three or four villages I have just mentioned accounted for the majority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what was their familiarity with the terrain of the area of -- their area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: The people who made up the battalion at the time, with the exception of the commander who is not a native of Prozor himself, he came from elsewhere, so these people who made up most of our unit were fully familiar with the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the people living in the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were familiar with the area. And the population, were they equally familiar with the population?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I'm not sure what you're driving at. What people are you talking about? If I'm talking about the people who made up the Independent Prozor Battalion, then I can tell you they were from Prozor municipality and they were familiar with the lie of the land.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And obviously if they came from that particular territory they would also know the people who reside in that territory. Would that be an accurate assessment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: In part, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of reputation did this -- these soldiers have, the soldiers of the Prozor Independent Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: I believe they were good soldiers, good fighters. I believe all their actions were determined by their commander. They obeyed their commander with no reservations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the commander of the Prozor Independent Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: There was several and there were frequent changes, but in the period under consideration it was Enver Buza. I heard that he was a native of the Visoko area. Visoko is a town near Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did he join the Prozor Independent Battalion, Enver Buza?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: I can't give you the exact date, but I believe it was sometime around May 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what impact did it have on the Prozor Independent Battalion when Enver Buza took over its command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: We drew a comparison between the previous commander and the one who is now there. At the outset, we were more than happy with his work and the way he ran the battalion. As compared to the previous commander, the improvement that he brought was mostly about improving the communications system. What used to be territorial units were now blended together. There were companies pertaining to each of the villages, Here, Kute, and Scipe. He detached the battalion command and moved it out of a settled area, thus making it entirely independent of what we referred to as the influence of the village locally. These were the good things he did. However, after that he started seeing his role in such a way that he believed he had absolute power and that he no longer answered to anyone; thus, to my mind at least, exceeding his authority and the powers that he had in actual fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what kind of relationship would you say he had with his subordinates?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: He had two of his friends in the battalion command, and he was only open to whatever suggestions came from those two. He ignored everyone else and refused any suggestions that came from elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was your relationship with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: At the beginning, the relationship was very good, but towards the end it was rapidly deteriorating until it came to a head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what do you mean it came to a head?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: There was a clash of opinions. There was a verbal clash. We couldn't go on working together. I requested to be relieved of my duties, which -- and he obliged with great pleasure. I was relieved of my duties in early 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the Prozor Independent Battalion based?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: First the command was based at Scipe, the headquarters. Later it was moved to a different house in the same village. And it was in spring or summer of 1993 that the command of the battalion was moved to Dobro Polje, a place called Dobro Polje. There was a hut there in the forest, and that was where the battalion commander and our communications centre were based.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to orient Their Honours to the exact location, I'd like you to see this photograph, please. It's 0299-2279. It will come up on your screen in a minute, Witness. While that's coming up, perhaps I'll take this opportunity to remind you that since you are a protected witness, would you be careful about saying anything that you feel may identify you in the course of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI 331.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you. May the photograph --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what this picture is of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: This photograph shows the hut. There was an outbuilding. There was an annex, which was torn down once the war was over. You can see the road leading to Prozor down the valley. The distance between the hut and Prozor is about 22 kilometres if you take the road that you can see in the photograph. If you take the opposite direction, it takes you to a mountain. If you go on down that road, you eventually reach Fojnica. And if you go past Fojnica, you reach a town that is already on the outskirts of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you please mark for me the hut which was your command. And what was this area called where this -- your command post was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: This is the hut.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was your command post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what's the area called itself where this command post was? Is it Dobro Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Everything you can see here is called Dobro Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's in Dobro Polje --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: But this area over here is called Rizak. There's a creek running here. You can't see it in the photograph, but it's there, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you go with me for a minute. Where you draw your circle, would you draw -- would you write command, C, or C and PID, which means the command post for the Prozor Independent Battalion.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where that arrow is, can you tell us which that's the direction towards? Would that be towards Here and Uzdol? Where you've drawn the arrow going --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: It's all the same. The entire building was in fact the command post, the place for the commander, and the communications centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. If you'll bear with me, please, Witness, this arrow that you've drawn, can you please generally -- so that Their Honours can follow your testimony as to where this arrow is pointing, which direction. So if you wanted to go to Uzdol it will be that arrow. So can you write there for me, please, to Uzdol.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you write on that arrow, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I please tender that into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: There's no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P331.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe the marked one and the original one are all admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And the original is P330 as well as.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. The original, Your Honours, is 331, and this marked one will be 332. If that's helpful.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Correct, Ms. Chana.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, would you tell us what kind of military actions would the Prozor Independent Battalion undertake mostly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: The Prozor Independent Battalion mostly engaged in defensive combat activities. It defended the area of Here, Scipe, Kute, and the territory of other small places in that area. However, it would occasionally also carry out reconnaissance and sabotage activities. This mainly involved infiltrating the enemy's rear in order to attack certain key features or to obtain information. Or sometimes the Bosniak civilian population in the summer of 1993 was withdrawn from that territory. They were wandering around the woods in that area and they were withdrawn and brought to our territory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would they mostly engage in inhabited areas or uninhabited areas?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: These actions, these activities, were mostly carried out in open fields apart from a number of actions. But usually these actions were carried out in open fields.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you please tell us, if you can cast your mind back to about October of 1992, and very briefly tell Their Honours what was happening at that time in Prozor.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: In the week that started on the 22nd of October, 1992 -- well, I don't know which day is Monday, I don't know which date Monday would be during that period. But on that day, on that date, tension suddenly escalated in Prozor because HVO units or Croatian army units that we weren't familiar with, we didn't know who was there, encircled Prozor. And at all the access routes to Prozor, they set up checkpoints at which they checked people and vehicles. You could feel this increased tension up until Thursday when a session of the War Presidency was scheduled in order to attempt to obtain an explanation from the Croatian side as to what was happening. At that meeting, certain explanations were provided, explanations that we found unacceptable. They said that this was happening because of certain problems in Novi Travnik and because of certain problems in Jajce. And we couldn't understand why it was necessary to encircle Prozor because of what I have just mentioned. And secondly, the beginning of the school year 1992/1993 was an issue that was raised because the Croatian side insisted that the school year should commence in accordance with the educational plans in force in the Republic of Croatia. At that meeting held on the 23rd of October they issued an ultimatum. They requested that the Bosnian side accept the way the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna be organised, accept its existence, and we couldn't accept it. It was a parastate. In addition, there was some sort of agreement that was reached at the meeting, an official agreement, according to which the checkpoints should be removed and to according to which the military units should be sent back to where they had come from. And all this was to be made official at a break that occurred at 1500 hours after the meeting. However, when the record was to be compiled after -- during the break, the president of the HDZ arrived and he said, You are negotiating but you are already killing people as a result. And he left as well as the entire delegation from the place where the meeting was being held. And five minutes later, the artillery started pounding the entire town very intensively. That was on the 23rd of October. And by 1200 hours on the following day, the HVO or the Croatian army, I don't know which units, some units from the outside, entered the town and certain -- some sort of an armoured unit consisting of 13 or 14 tanks also entered the town. The Territorial Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina then lost control of the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, by September 1993, how much of the territory was occupied by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: By September 1993, the HVO had occupied perhaps 85 or 90 per cent of the territory of the municipality of Prozor. There was only a pocket that remained in the north-eastern or eastern part of the municipality. The places of Here, Kute, and Scipe were concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to the Bosniak population in Prozor after the HVO occupied it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: The Bosniak population was gathered, was assembled, in collection centres. Certain investigations were made. People were forced to sign certain statements, claiming that extremists, Muslim extremists, were responsible for certain conflicts, et cetera. During that time, the territory under the control of the HVO was a territory in which the Bosniak population had been completely destroyed, because of out of 7.400 Bosniaks living in the municipality in 1991, 128 Bosniaks remained in an area in Prozor itself. Six individuals remained in Duge, and the Delic family remained in the Orasac settlement. Those are the only people who remained out of the 7.000 people by September 1993. During that time -- at that time, we had a list of 181 people who had gone missing. 968 military-able men were in camps at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us about an incident which happened in July of 1993 in respect of some Bosnian prisoners.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In July of 1993. Could you tell us about an incident which happened about Bosnian prisoners.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: In the town of Prozor, there was a collection centre in which there was several hundred prisoners; that was in the building of the secondary school. Upon the 31st of July, 1993, the ABiH carried out an action in the Crni Vrh area. That is a mountain to the north-east of Prozor. Members of the Prozor Independent Battalion and other units participated in that action, other units of the ABiH. On that day, the defence lines of the HVO were practically destroyed. Our units advanced towards the Makljen pass, which is an important position because the main road from Mostar and Banja Luka and Zagreb comes to a junction there. And after those lines had been broken through, there are about 90 camp inmates from the secondary school in Prozor were assembled. And three chains of them were formed and they were used against the ABiH. Two chains were used in the Crni Vrh area, and one in the direction towards Gornji Vakuf. One of those chains of inmates, 24 Bosniaks, 24 able-bodied Bosniaks, were killed. According to the statements of the survivors, they were shot in the back; that's how they were killed. The second chain of inmates managed to pull out and moved over to our side in the course of those actions. I saw those people and I spoke to them. None of them had footwear. They were all barefoot. When fleeing, they had lost their footwear. The third chain of inmates was used in the following way: One man who had been imprisoned in the secondary school drove a bulldozer, and behind him this live shield, this chain of inmates, progressed and ABiH members opened fire and wounded them. He then fled somewhere and that's how the action ended. Although a military policeman threatened to kill them all if they survived once he returned. That's what I could tell you about the incident on the 31st of July. There's one other important thing. On that day, an HVO member went to the village of Lapsunj, which is about two kilometres from the town, and he killed a nine-month-old child and the child's mother. His name is Haris Pilav, and his mother's name was Semsa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. -- I'm sorry, but thank you, Witness. To be quite clear, what do you mean by a chain, very briefly, please? When you referred to a chain, what exactly did you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: I meant that on that day the HVO used a live shield formed of individuals who had been captured in the course of combat. One such human chain was killed. They were buried in a mass grave and then moved to another village, and when exhumed they were found in that place. They were all identified -- not all of them in fact. 20 of them were identified; four of them could not be identified because this was not possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that's fine. Now, did some of these prisoners, these Bosnians who had been used as human shields escape and join the Prozor Independent Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: The second human shield, the second human chain, that survived, most of them all volunteered to join the Prozor Independent Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you please tell us, these soldiers who had been used as human shields and who joined the Prozor Independent Battalion, what was their general attitude?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: I spoke to some of them. I spoke about the tragedy that had struck them. Their position, however, was that they would fight to the very end against the HVO because the human shield is not the only experience they had had. Many people had been taken away from that secondary school. Some were executed at a rubbish dump, and they were never found because the rubbish dump is not an orderly one and it's always on fire. Many people were humiliated. Many women and girls were raped at the time. That was their position -- not only their position but it was a position shared by it was an opinion shared by all of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By "all of us" you mean the entire Prozor Independent Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what happened on that particular date? Yes, I would like to remind you, Witness, that since you have asked for protective measures and if you say certain things, it would be very easy to identify who you are. So I would remind you once again to please -- if -- not say what you just said about your position.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: If that could be redacted, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, the witness shouldn't be put in a position of having to sculpt his evidence. If there's sensitive evidence to be given, he should be given the chance to say what he has to say, and therefore we don't object to the matter going into private session. If sensitive material is going to be elicited, then the Witness should be given the full chance to answer properly. That would be an appropriate course if that's going to happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. But on that occasion we haven't come to the sensitive part yet; it's just beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, frankly I agree -- I agree with what Your Honour says, and I'm not objecting to what my learned friend just said there; it was quite proper. But if we're going to come to an area where it's likely that some parts of his evidence will be sensitive and some parts not, and the witness is here to say what he saw and what he knows, so let him say it and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, just to give an indication to counsel, and I think I know what he's referring to. The Prosecution has no intention of leading such evidence. The witness is available to the Defence to lead the evidence they want, irrespective of these sensitive issues. That's about as coded a message as I can give, Your Honour, without betraying what we are saying, but....

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we'll see.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us on that day, 5th September, 1993, what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: I was in the command of the Prozor Independent Battalion on that day. I couldn't really say whether it was on the 5th, 4th, or 6th of September, since a lot of time has passed since then, but I think it was around that time. General Halilovic came to our command post with some other commanders, and they held a meeting with our commander, Enver Buza. We walked around that building and waited to see what would happen. They had that meeting. General Halilovic came on that occasion. And on that time -- on that occasion he -- or during that period he came twice or perhaps three times. And I remember during one of his meetings that area was shelled by the artillery. I don't know whether that was during his first visit or during his second visit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But can we take this a little slower, if I may. Could you tell us who accompanied General Halilovic when he arrived on that first time he came, as you said around the 5th sometime?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: On that occasion, he had his escort with him. There was the journalist, Sefko Hodzic. There was some commanders. I think Haso Hakolovic was there, the commander of the 45th Brigade. And I think there were some commanders of certain brigades. I can't remember which brigades, but there were those commanders. Perhaps Selmo Cikotic, the commander of an operative group, was also there. But I'm not sure. I know there were all of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the commander of the 6th Corps there, Salko Gusic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: I think so. But he also came during that period; that's certain. I don't know whether he came on the first visit or the second one, but he came for sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on this particular time, was this the first time you had seen General Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: In person, yes. I had seen him before that time on television when we had electricity in 1992 and 1993. I knew him, as I had seen him on television, and I recognised him immediately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you present at this particular meeting that he held with your commander, Enver Buza?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: I wasn't present at that meeting. I wasn't in the room where the meeting was held. But afterwards, we were summoned by the commander. He summoned his assistants and provided information about what had been discussed at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did your commander, Enver Buza, say about what had transpired at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours -- sorry. May I just intervene here. Your Honours, I haven't risen up until now. There is no objection to hearsay as such at this Tribunal, of course. But I should mention this once again. The Prosecution have made a specific decision to withdraw Enver Buza from the witness list, so therefore I object to evidence being given about what Mr. Buza said. I should indicate that, Your Honours, I've made a similar objection in the past in relation to one witness. Your Honours ruled against me on that occasion, and I've got nothing different to say in justification this time. So effectively I just want to put that on the record that generally, as a matter of policy, we object to such questions, not just with this witness, of course, but across the board. But having made the objection, I understand what the answer is likely to be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes. And I think in this Tribunal the hearsay evidence is admissible. Of course we'll consider your objections when we evaluate this piece of the evidence. You may proceed, Ms. Chana.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: I'm obliged, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Can you tell us what Enver Buza said to you after the meeting with Halilovic and crew?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: On that occasion he told us that the time had come to finally liberate Prozor, that the time had come for the state to assist us in some way. He said that everyone in our vicinity would be assisting us. Our units in the vicinity would also assist us to finally liberate Prozor, and the time had come for us to go swimming in the Rama lake, which is on the other side of the municipality. These are the sort of things that he said, and he said that it would be a large-scale operation led by General Halilovic, the Chief of Staff. That was the exact position that he had at the time as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when he said that General Halilovic was to lead this operation, what did you understand by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Well, I took that to mean what I have just said. General Halilovic was, in my opinion, a figure of authority at the time because until recently he had practically been the commander of the ABiH, and he was the highest-ranking officer from your army and he was with us. And he gave us hope. We hoped that everything would unfold in the way that they had said things would unfold. So he really was a figure of authority for us. There was no doubt about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was Halilovic's position in the army as you understood it at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: We received information perhaps a month or two previously - I can't remember exactly when - according to which commander of the General Staff had been appointed or commander of the supreme command; I can't remember the exact name because the name changed. However, the Chief of Staff was General Halilovic; he remained the Chief of Staff. As far as official explanations are concerned, we received an explanation according to which the Main Staff of the army was finally being established that no one was being replaced, no system was being replaced. It was a matter of strengthening the organisation and of establishing the final structure and bringing it up to strength, establishing the final structure of the Main Staff. So even without such an explanation, we considered Sefer Halilovic to be a figure of authority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was this news that you were to participate in the operation to liberate Prozor good news for yourself and the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: It was good news for us, yes. We were happy about it and we very much supported this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, later on did you -- what was your understanding of the relationship between Halilovic and Delic vis-a-vis these -- this restructuring of the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: At the time these changes occurred, we knew nothing. We only had whatever official information was available; that was all we had. We accepted it as such. It was later, however, that I learned that there had been other reasons for the appointment of a commander whose remit was to restrict the powers of the Chief of Staff. The word was there was a clash between the Sandzak and the Bosniak factions in the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and their diverging policies. This, however, was mere hearsay; this was never corroborated. And all of this needs to be taken with more than just the proverbial grain of salt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So was Halilovic's authority ever questioned in your -- in your presence at any time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were you told what the main goal of this operation was going to be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: The main goal of the operation from our point of view was to regain Prozor; that was our local objective. Secondly, I think people were saying at the time that the HVO had exceeded the extent to which their armed units could be tolerated in Bosnia and Herzegovina, generally speaking. Attacks had started mounting by the HVO on that day. There had been orders for the army to be disarmed and resubordinated to the HVO. We knew about this. This made it impossible to avoid this unfortunate war, the operations that ensued, and the domino effect that was triggered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you tell me whether General Halilovic came to your command post again sometime later, and when that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: He came on the eve of the action. I think he only stayed briefly. We were told at the time that he was just passing through on his way to Voljevac, a village in Gornji Vakuf municipality. The units in that area were on the right flank neighbouring the Prozor Independent Battalion. Final talks were under way on the exact modality that the operation was to take.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Can you -- I want to ask you if you could try to, please, pinpoint a date. I know it's been sometime. But if the first meeting happened at about 5th, how many days after did Sefer Halilovic come to Dobro Polje again? Was it a few days? Five days? Six days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Something like that. I believe six or seven days later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And what happened when he came at that time? Who did he meet with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Needless to say, he met with the commander. I don't remember all these details very clearly. It's been over 12 years since. I know that there was an ongoing debate in our command about the axis down which the Prozor Independent Battalion would be moving. What I can tell you about that is: Once I entered the commander's office - I said this in my statement about six months ago, and that's exactly how it happened - I saw an order to attack. This order was signed by General Sefer Halilovic. The order precisely defined the axis of attack of the Prozor Independent Battalion, and that's what I wanted to know about. The axis was Crni Vrh, Makljen. I don't think there was any reference whatsoever to the village of Uzdol in that document. Although I was in no position to study the document, I looked through it briefly and quickly. This was a highly confidential document, and by rights I should not -- I should never have had an opportunity to even see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you look at it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Human curiosity, that's all. I wanted to know where our unit would be going. I couldn't resist the urge to have a look.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Now I want to show you a document and then I'll ask you some questions. This is P124; it will come up on your screen in a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: -- inquire whether this is the document that's the order dated the 15th of September that's being brought up?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe so, because it appears on our screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's very well. Well, I might have something to raise about this in a minute, but we'll see what occurs. But we received proofing notes, Your Honour -- anyway, I'll -- I'm obliged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed, Ms. Chana.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you look at this document and see whether you recognise it. First of all, what kind of a document is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: This is an order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Well, it's stated in the upper left corner. The document clearly indicates that. Secondly, 12 or 13 years have gone by. It's difficult for me to confirm that this is the document that I saw at the time. If it is not the same document, then it is very much like it. I told you about the circumstances under which I saw the document. I can't be entirely certain that I was able to go through the entire document nor am I able to remember the entire document now. It might have been something like this one. I took that document to be an attack order or an order defining the axis of attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you look the task part, is that what you understood at that time what the Prozor -- what the Prozor Independent Battalion was going to be -- and the line of attack for the Prozor Independent Battalion?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I'll object to that. Your Honour, this is now -- the purpose of this particular line of questioning is quite clear, but the witness has said that he can't say that this is the document that he looked at. I've got no objection to my friend asking what this witness understood to be Buza's instructions, if there were any, at the time. But by doing it with reference to this document now it's not proper, now that the witness has given the answer that he's given about this document. He's not saying it's the document he saw. So that he shouldn't be asked questions about that document in the way it's being done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the witness is not a hundred per cent sure about this document, whether it is that document that he saw at the time, but the witness testified that he saw a similar document to this aspect. I believe the Prosecution is entitled to go along this line. First of all, we'll come to the contents of this document, and them later on we'll see how much weight we should put to this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you look at the task part and see whether that was the line of attack as you understood it after looking at the document at the time that the Prozor Independent Battalion was going to take?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just a minute. Now, Your Honours, that question has now contained -- I'm sorry for interrupting, Witness. There's a legal objection I'm taking to the question. Your Honours, if you look the question there it says: "As you understood it after looking at the document at the time." Now, that's the very thing that the witness hasn't agreed that he did. So I object to that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I think this objection has merits.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was simply asking the witness to clarify what he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that this witness said that he was not sure whether this is a document he saw at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, quite sure -- yes, Your Honour. If I -- let's see if I can ask the witness this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time you said you looked at this document, which was a combat order from General Halilovic, you wanted to know the line of attack. That was your main interest. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, sorry, again I object. There's a couple of assumptions built in there. There's a number of objections. I wouldn't object -- I can indicate this: I wouldn't object to the witness being asked about the document he did see at the time. That's fine. As long as there's no things like combat order built into the question. The witness could just be asked what did he see in that document and what he understood. How -- well, I won't design the question. But my objection is really to building in those extra clauses into it. So perhaps that would assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe, Ms. Chana, you could establish your case step by step.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you said you saw a document in Enver Buza's office, what kind of a document was it? Don't look at this document now. Just tell us what kind of a document was it? What was the nature of that document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: I told you that I had only seen the document in a hurry and I didn't go through the entire document. I can't say anything about its specific nature. All I was looking for was the section that pertained to the Prozor Independent Battalion. Everything else mattered a great deal less. I realised that the Prozor Independent Battalion was to move down the Crni Vrh-Makljen axis, and that was all I wanted to know. As soon as I saw that, I stopped reading the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, clarify this for me when you say that you were interested to see -- I want to be quite accurate here so I don't get an objection, was to move down. Can you define "move down," please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Moving where? What exactly do you want me to define?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said "move down," Witness, that you were interested to have a look at that document to see move down, where the Prozor Battalion was going to move down. We just want the Court to understand what you mean by "move down."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: When I said that, I meant that the Prozor Independent Battalion would use this axis that I mentioned to carry out an attack and that the superior command would determine who would be on the battalion's left and right flanks. When I use the word "to move," that's to mean moving in combat, and the reference is to an axis along which troops advanced to take a certain area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this was in respect of the military operation?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, once again I have to object; this time it's to a leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the witness said that to move, that is to -- that is to mean moving in combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Your Honours, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So -- which, you know, implies the military operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Of course it does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So I believe that this question was not a leading one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It's really the term "operation" that concerned me there, bearing in mind it's not this witness's evidence directly, but you have to decide other matters with reference to the word "operation." Military actions, I don't have any objection to that. I'm not trying to suggest that they were going there for a picnic, Your Honour. So that's not my objection. It was really the use of the word "operation." It may be that it's not crucial to my friend's question anyway. But that was what the objection was. It was that word "operation."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe -- at this stage I don't see the difference between operation and action. But if possible, Ms. Chana, you can use action instead of operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. But the witness has already stated earlier that there was a defensive plan to liberate Prozor, and I call that an operation. I'm not giving it a name. I'm just saying it's a military operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, that is kind of military or legal characterisation of that act. So at this stage we may use quite a neutral terminology.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, when you were looking at that document to see where your line of combat was to be, were there other units or was yours the only unit reflected in that particular order that you saw lying Enver Buza's desk?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I object to the term "order" being used, frankly. The witness has indicated he's not sure of precisely the nature of this document. Now, I don't want these assumptions to be built into questions. So I object to that on the basis of using the term "order."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, now we'll come to this document and first of all, Ms. Chana, you have to establish whether this document is an order or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness has indicated previously, and I will quote from his evidence, which is just given, "this order was signed by General Sefer Halilovic," this order that he saw. He did use the word "order," Your Honour. This is going to confuse the witness. He's used the word "order."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I understand. I mean that the document -- the witness was referring the document he saw at that time. Here we come to this piece of document and document 214.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So we have to establish whether document 214 is an order or not in the view of the witness, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you look at the document, Witness, this document now on your screen. What would you categorise this document to be, if you just look at it with your knowledge of military affairs? If you look at the beginning it says -- does it say "order number"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is it? Can you please -- to be quite clear for the Chamber, what would you categorise this document to be, the one on your screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: I believe the document reflects its own substance in no uncertain terms. I believe it would be superfluous for me to comment on that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Superfluous or not, Witness, would you please comment on it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: This document shows in the upper left corner, and it was produced by the supreme command Main Staff. It was produced in Voljevac on the 15th of September, 1993. It speaks about some tactical plans as I see in the second half of the document. It's in reference to a number of units, the Prozor Independent Battalion, the Sutjeska Battalion, parts of the elements of the 45th Brigade. There you have it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it -- is it a document entitled "order number"? Does it say that? Can you read that, please, at the front of the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, again -- well, no, perhaps I'll just let the witness answer. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. What I know based on my experience with administration is that this document was dated. But I have no idea about this reference number. I can't tell you what it means exactly. It is clearly stated that this document is an order containing all the relevant elements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the relevant elements, what are the relevant elements, Witness? Is this a combat order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Can I have a minute to go through it a little more carefully?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Please take your time.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Perhaps, Your Honour, we can give a break at this time and the witness can read it at the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's a good idea. Any objections, Mr. Morrissey? I saw you --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. There's an objection -- there's something I'm going to raise later on, but I think if the Prosecutor wants to proceed this way, she's entitled to proceed as she chooses. I don't have any objection to the witness being given any documents he chooses to look at properly so that he can be -- give his answers after 12 years in full knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll have a break now and we'll resume at 11.00 sharp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Chana, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, before the break we were looking at this document P124, which I think you have the Bosnian version before you because it was given to you during the break to study. Have you now had a chance to look at it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: I had a look at the document, and I thank you for allowing me to think about it a little during the break.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what have you thought about it? Would you like to tell us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: When compared to the usual form of correspondence between the higher- and lower-level commander in the ABiH, there are certain differences. It differs from a textbook example of an order, such as it is issued to a subordinate commander. So I can say that an order issued in the ABiH didn't contain a reference to the person sent to in the middle. And in this part which -- where it says order, you don't -- it doesn't say "order," it says "I hereby order." When this term is used in our language, it has far greater binding force. So when compared with the standard types of orders issued, these are the differences that I can observe. But this document does contain all the other elements, because in the lower left-hand corner it says who it was addressed to; it was addressed to the person concerned by the order. So this document does contain all these relevant elements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to go back to when you first went into Enver Buza's office and you saw a piece of paper lying on his desk. You said you were curious, human curiosity, and you wanted to know where the Prozor Independent Battalion was going to attack. Now, what made you see that piece of paper on Mr. -- Enver Buza's desk and know that this document is going to give you that information? What was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Well, there are a lot of rumours about what would happen during that period of time. We were expecting an order to arrive, an order issued by someone, or we were expecting instructions to arrive. We were expecting something to happen, so these things were expected. And secondly, I don't know how this document arrived. I don't know whether someone delivered it personally or whether it was forwarded through the communications equipment that we also had. This equipment was fairly reliable and well-protected. As I said, I don't know how the document arrived. I don't know whether it was delivered by someone personally or whether it was forwarded through the communications equipment that we had. When I saw this piece of paper on the desk, I knew what it was immediately. I read through it and I tried to see whether Prozor Battalion had to engage in action. To tell you the truth, in this first part of the document you have certain tactical axes that are indicated but the task mentioned below -- well, perhaps I didn't even read through the entire document at that time because all I was interested in was the Prozor Battalion. So I could not say for certain that this is the document I saw. There are a lot of details that I cannot even remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. But in respect of the Prozor Independent Battalion and their task during this offensive, is it the same that you recall then as you see in this document now which I've shown to you in court? Was it the same task that you observed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: I can only tell you about how I understood the task on the basis of what I read in that document and in comparison to what subsequently transpired. I cannot compare this document with the other document. During that period of time, certain alternatives were discussed and the possibility of changing the axis that the Prozor Independent Battalion would use to break through. These matters were discussed in our command, but in the end the final decision in an army is always taken by the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you looked at the document at the time, what was your understanding as to where your unit was going to go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: On the basis of that document, I thought that the entire Prozor Battalion had to take the Crni Vrh-Makljen axis. I believed that was the axis they had to attack along. That's a mountainous chain to the north-east and to the north of the town of Prozor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it consistent with this document that you see now, that task?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, with the greatest respect, this is impermissible. It's not a question for this witness to say whether it's consistent or not. It's a question for you, the Tribunal, to draw an inference at a later time on that topic. I'm going to make it quite clear now that I'll cross-examine this witness on what documents he's been shown and whether he's been given a proper chance to consider all the documents that are relevant to this, whether there's something funny going on in the court right now. So I make that clear so my friend has every opportunity to deal with the issue in evidence in-chief because it is a matter that I'm going to deal with. But in any event, I object to that opinion being sought of the witness here. Whether it's consistent or not consistent, that's your job, with respect, not that of the witness..

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Chana, we could read the document ourself and compare it with the testimony of this witness at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think this issue is self-evident.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'm obliged for your guidance and I will seek the protection of the Court in respect of the remark just made by the learned friend. That there's something funny going on is an innuendo which I must not allow to remain unanswered. I mean, I am not quite aware as to what he is alluding to that there is something funny going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'll explain it if you want me to explain it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, very well. Well, Your Honours, at the moment it appears that the witness is being asked to comment upon this document, in spite of the clear date that's on it, with a view he's now given his answers on three or four occasions and so I would submit that he's now fully answered the question. He can't say this is the document that he saw. The Prosecutor wants you to draw an inference, obviously, that that is the document he saw, despite the date that's on it. Now despite the fact that my learned friend hasn't yet asked him what the date of the Uzdol attack of course was. Now, Your Honours, I've got a lot to say about this. But Your Honours -- and I don't want to make the objection a speech in front of the witness, frankly. Perhaps I can do it this way. Your Honours have seen a number of other documents that have been tendered in this case. One of them was a document very similar to the one that is now before the witness, and on one view it may have been a draft of it, but it's a different document; it's the document produced by Vehbija Karic, and -- but with Halilovic's name on the bottom. That was tendered as a separate exhibit, got the same date on it, 15th. There are other orders, which I'll put to this witness myself, concerning who was issuing orders and in respect of which orders Enver Buza said he was acting when he produced that combat report that's been tendered in evidence Now, I don't know whether those were shown to the witness yet or not. That's why I mention it now to give the Prosecutor fair warning that I'm going to raise it. Because again, the witness is here, I don't wish to go into the specific criticisms I have to make. But I hope that clarifies what I'm pointing to what when I say that there's something funny. That's what I'm getting at, that there's been a -- Do you want me to go on with the witness here, Your Honour? I'm a bit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think I've heard your positions already. And I believe that you will have the full opportunity to cross-examine this witness on all those documents related to that. Ms. Chana, maybe you could establish the relevance of this document to our case which mainly happened in Uzdol. So from the date of this document, this document was issued after what happened in Uzdol. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, this is the purported date. There is going to be evidence, Your Honour, that this is not the correct date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you have to present your evidence to show us --

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Not necessarily from this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But at least at this stage you have to establish a certain relevance on that, to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I will certainly ask the witness about the date and see -- we'll hear from what he says, but I still feel that the words used by my learned friend were unfortunate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I quite understand that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, this document that you can see on the screen, this P124, what is the date of this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: I can't see the date on the screen, but I have the paper copy and it says that the date is the 15th of September, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us when was the first -- the attack? Just the date for now, please, because we are trying to establish date here.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: The attack on Uzdol was on the 14th of September, in the morning. It was on the 14th of September.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, having said that and after having looked at the document, would you say that this is a correct date?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, how could the witness possibly answer that question? He has said that he doesn't know if this is the document that he saw or not. That's his clear evidence. And if he's then asked if that's a correct -- if that's the right date on the document, then, in my submission, it's asking him to give a guess on something that he has already said that he can't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, but the witness certified that he saw a similar document, if not this one. I believe that the witness was someone in that battalion and the incident was -- happened before that date, and that battalion took part in that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: -- Operation or action.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So I believe that the witness could give us his opinion on that. But we'll bear in mind your objections on this very issue and see how far we could go.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Witness, given the content of this document, would you say that was a correct date, given that the combat itself started on the 13th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: All I can say is that one might say that on the 15th of September there was still ongoing combat. Combat only ceased a couple days later, but combat commenced on the 13th; I can confirm that. These are facts. This document is dated the 15th of September, and that's what I can say. I don't know what else you could expect of me in relation to this matter because these are the facts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, thank you, Witness, for that assistance. Now I will move on from there. Can you tell us what happened immediately afterwards? This is now -- we -- just to remind you, this is after you have seen this order from Enver Buza. What happens next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: After that we had certain discussions and spoke to unit commanders to see what our axes of attacks might be and to see what some of our officers had proposed to try and determine which axis would be the most suitable one to break through. Since our units had previously carried out combat activities along this axis and they had a certain amount of experience and it was difficult for them in -- the most resistant defence lines of the HVO were there, their attempts to change the situation, and I said that the commander took the final decision. And I don't know to whom he could have forwarded such a proposal to have it accepted and adopted. Afterwards, there was some other agreements that I can't remember exactly. I know that the final plan for action was one we became familiar with, not before the 12th of September. Then that is when we knew our exact axis of attack, perhaps a day before the action itself was carried out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just to be clear, originally your understanding of the axis was the direction of Makljen and Crni Vrh. Is that correct? That was your first information about your axis.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then it apparently changed to Uzdol and Gradina. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: No, not quite. Because -- this is what finally happened because part of our units were engaged along the Crni Vrh-Makljen axis, but not fully. That is something that had been changed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then finally, what was your main target of attack? Which axis were you, the Prozor Independent Battalion, supposed to engage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: The Independent Prozor Battalion was supposed to provide a company of assistance along the Crni Vrh-Makljen axis, that unit. It was sent to carry out its task. The second axis was Uzdol, and objective was to destroy the military capacity of the HVO in that village and its immediate surroundings. The military capacity of the HVO, if I need to mention this, consisted of one battalion which was in that area, a command post in the building of the primary school, a communications centre, a mortar battery of various calibres. The mortars were deployed at several locations, but there was an entire battery by the primary school building. There were also two tanks, one by the primary school building and another at another location called Kranjcici. That objective was excluded at the very last minute. Those were the targets, the objectives. And another objective was to break through at the front line, at the HVO front line, where they had entrenched several locations or they had fortified positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in order to assist you and to explain to Their Learned Judges, I will show you some photographs. And I will first show you 0299-2306. There will be a photograph coming up.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI 333.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us from which direction this photograph has been taken? Perhaps we will use Here as the point. Can you tell us where Here is there, please. Would you put a circle around it and then you can write on it -- you'll be assisted in a minute.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And under whose control was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: That place was under the ABiH -- under the control of the ABiH, under the control of the Prozor Independent Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Now, can you tell us where -- which side would be Kriz, which is part of Uzdol? Can you please draw a circle there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Kriz would be here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you drew an arrow as to where -- which -- where was the school, which direction from Kriz was the school where the HVO military base was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you would be having -- you would have to come from Here, across Kriz, to Uzdol? Was that the line? I'll show you another photograph in a minute to make it clearer, but this is just to orientate Their Honours. Yes. Where you've written "Here," can you please write "ABiH," so we know whose control that was under.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's right. And would you please mark there "Kriz" in the other circle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you also circle for us the hill of Krstiste.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you write there K -- KR would be sufficient.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And under whose control was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you speak it out for the record, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: It was under the control of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. It was in fact a hill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I'd like you to see -- put --

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, can that be introduced into evidence, the original and the marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. It is admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The original will be Prosecution Exhibit P333, and the one that is marked will be Prosecution Exhibit P334.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I would like to show you 0299-2292. Again, is this the same photograph from the other side.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: I can see the same photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry. Can you see the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes. This photograph was shot from the direction of Here towards Uzdol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you circle Here.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you write in there "Here," please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you could circle the Krstiste hill again, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you also put in there Gradina hill.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under whose control was Gradina hill?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Under the control of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you -- yes. Yes. Where you've put GR it would be mixed up with Kriz. Can you put a T next to the KR so we know it's not Kriz.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us from that road, if you can do an arrow, as to where -- which direction the PIB was, the Prozor Independent Battalion.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you put PIB there, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many kilometres would you have to go down that road before you reached your command post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: About 10 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You -- where there's -- where you've put KR, can you put a T there, please, that Krstiste hill, can you put a T there, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: I just have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. You put it in a wrong place when you put Gradina hill. I want you to put it where the Krstiste hill is, KRT.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And in fact if you can blank out the T of the Gradina.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: How do you do that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If the assistant can do that. Just rub it out. Yeah, just squiggle on it. Thank you. We'll come back to these pictures in a minute. Now --

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, I would like to tender these two photographs, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: There's no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. They are admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The original is Prosecution Exhibit P335, and the one that's marked Prosecution Exhibit P336.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can I take you to the night of the 12th to 13th September, please. What happened in that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: The night of the 12th to 13th September, based on information that we had, the operation commenced. We heard sounds of fierce fighting along the Crni Vrh-Makljen axis. We were far enough, or rather near enough to hear the sounds of battle clearly. However, the units of our battalion did not move. There had to be an order by the commander personally to start moving, and I mean Enver Buza himself. He simply didn't do that. We just stuck around anxiously awaiting his orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know which units started this attack that you heard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: We know that units of the 317th Brigade from Gornji Vakuf and the 45th Brigade were in those positions where the sounds of fighting were coming from. We had also received word that units of OG West had commenced an operation along their own axis successfully and that they were then redirected.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you saw that you were not -- you hadn't been given an order to go into battle yourself, did you ask Enver Buza what was happening, what was the position of all the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: We asked no questions; we just awaited our orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on 13th September, did anyone come to visit your command post in Dobro Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: General Halilovic himself came. I believe this was sometime in the afternoon. It was certainly past noon. He was disappointed and angry that we were even there, so angry and disappointed in fact that he walked into our commander's office and started yelling at him. He made threats, saying that -- I'm not sure how I should put it. What the commander was doing was an act of idiocy, that he should have joined in the action at the same time as everyone had set off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were present at this -- at this time. How many others were present when General Halilovic was angry at Buza?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: There was several people from the command. I believe five or six of our people were there. He made some excuses, which we didn't understand to be quite honest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: He said we had not been given fuel and gave that as the reason why the battalion had not joined the operation -- I mean Commander Buza. He was the one who provided explanations to General Halilovic. In our eyes, he could not have fallen any lower. This was a flimsy excuse. He was just looking for an excuse, but we in fact knew that that could not have been the reason.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Witness, I know it's been sometime since this happened, but could you please try to remember exactly what it was that Commander Halilovic said to Buza.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: He said he would kill him unless he finally sent his battalion into action.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anything else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: He must have, but I can't recall exactly. This is something that is lodged in my memory. I can't remember anything else. Our commander answered back. He gave some reasons. He talked about fuel. I believe he mentioned food as well. But we certainly weren't short of food, so that can't have been a proper reason.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you think was the reason that Enver Buza didn't engage his unit in battle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: I think the chief reason was that he was not up to scratch. He wasn't able to deal with the situation. He had lost it and was scared. He was no soldier, not in terms of his talent, not in terms of his professional training. I believe that was the chief reason he failed to do anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did Halilovic do next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: He requested the commander to gather all our units. We assembled in front of the hut that you could see in that first photograph that was shown. He gave a brief, a rather measured speech. I can say now he seemed an entirely different person, bearing in mind how he had treated the commander previously. He gave a brief speech lasting perhaps about five or ten minutes. I can't remember every single thing he said, but I can say what I remember. First of all, he said we were late and that this was impermissible. He said the chief objective was to crush the HVO and to liberate Prozor. He said we were expected to do our utmost and fight to regain Prozor, as all the others were doing as we spoke. And we could hear sounds of fighting around Crni Vrh. He said we would be entering a settled area, which required a different method of combat. He said this was a far more dangerous type of combat. He said we should be careful, but he said we should be - and I'm quoting - sharp and soldierly, that we should behave in a sharp and soldierly way. He said brave, too. And he told us again to be very careful. That is more or less what he said. Once he finished speaking, we realised the -- how serious the situation was. He left soon after. But perhaps about an hour later our own commander summoned our units and gave an emotional speech, yelling and shouting. He was out to regain his reputation in our eyes, I suppose. He gave a speech.
