utterances.text: Yes, very well. Well, the -- I want to show it to him and I want to ask him whether Sefer Halilovic appeared to exercise the powers that are in that order. But if my friend says that I shouldn't be showing the witness a document that he's not sure that he's seen before in court, well of course that's a legitimate objection to take and I won't show it to him. I'll ask him some other questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were proofed in this matter -- when you came to The Hague, what documents were you shown in proofing, to the best of your memory, Witness G?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: I was shown two documents. One was the document that I looked at a while ago, and there was another document produced by the command of the 317th Brigade on how combat operations were to be carried out. This other document was signed by Brigade Commander Zejnilagic. I can't remember his first name. Enver, Enver Zejnilagic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You weren't shown, by any chance, a combat report by the commander of the actual Prozor Independent Battalion itself, Enver Buza, concerning the action in Uzdol? They didn't show you that one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, in about 30 minutes I'll show it to you and we'll see what happens then. You've had your chance to comment upon it, if you've seen it before, if you have anything to say about it. But meanwhile, however, I'll press on. Now, I'd just like you to look at another document, and this is a document that's sitting right next to you now -- sorry, it's behind you. It's the map. There's a map there, a big map on an easel board. Do you see that, headed Operation Neretva.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That, I believe, is D131, Your Honours, and I express my gratitude, as always, to the court staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just having a look at that document there, does that appear to you to be a military map which has got the writing on it in the top left-hand corner "odobravam," "I have approved it," by Rasim Delic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, sorry. The question is simply: Does that appear to you to be a military map entitled Operacija Neretva, which has been authorised with the word "I have approved it," "odobravam" that is, in the top left-hand corner, above the name of the commander, Rasim Delic? I should ask: Are you able to read it from where you're sitting there, my first question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes, I see that now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks. And can you further see -- yes, I'm grateful to the court staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, my assistant just pointed out very sensibly to me that we don't want the witness to have to stand up because it means that it will go around the screens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, on that section we could go to the private session because, you know, the camera will focus on the map. I'm afraid that we'll disclose the identity of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, just I'm unaware of how it works, Your Honour, so perhaps for caution, I agree, perhaps we should go to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe we could go to private session now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So sorry, the question probably got lost in all the subordinate requests, and I'll just ask it again. Do the lines on that map, even though it's drawn at a high level, broadly reflect the combat operations which actually took place to your understanding on the 13th and 14th of September?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: I can say the map reflects what happened in the north sector, to the north of Jablanica, which is an area that I am fully familiar with. As concerns the area south of Jablanica, I really don't know who acted there, and this is not something that I wish to comment on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, it's not something I wish to trouble you with either, so we'll leave that topic there. Okay, well, thank you for that. Now, as to that map, I want to ask you this: Were you personally present down in Jablanica on the 4th of September when that map was signed under the word "odobravam" by Rasim Delic in the top left corner and counter-signed by the Chief of Staff, Sefer Halilovic, in the bottom right-hand corner? Were you present when that happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: I don't think I was present, or at least, I don't recall being present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did it come to your -- were you told by Commander Buza that Rasim Delic had -- had come to Herzegovina and held a meeting in Jablanica and signed and authorised that map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Commander Buza never told us. I did tell you about his style of sharing information. He failed to tell us about this, and the same applies to a great number of other things that we were supposed to know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And, look, I'm grateful for your patience in dealing with these questions. You have answered it in a general way, but I have to put some specifics to you, unfortunately, as I go through. But in any event I'll press on with those now. The next thing I want to ask you about is a meeting that took place at Dobro Polje, the headquarters of the Independent Prozor Battalion. Now, you've indicated that you were not present at the -- you were not present inside the room, but you were told what happened by Commander Buza. And I want to ask you this: Did you find that Commander Buza always told you things in an accurate and reliable way? In other words, did he always give you accurate and reliable information about the things he was telling you about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: I think it could be said that he provided us with superficial information. It was never thorough. From my present perspective, I can claim that what he fed us at the time was incomplete information at best. A lot was being left unsaid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, as to the commanders who were -- who you noticed to be present at that meeting, can I put some names to you and you can confirm whether or not you recall them being there. First of all, Salko Gusic, was he present at that meeting at Dobro Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. What about the his deputy commander, Bahrudin Fazlic? Do you recall whether he was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: I can't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether Haso Hakalovic, the commander of the 45th Neretvica Brigade was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Selmo Cikotic of Operations Group West?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Mr. Cikotic came several times and I believe he was present at the meeting, but I can say with a great degree of certainty that this was not the only time he was around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly. What about Vehbija Karic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: I don't think he was there at the meeting, but I'm not entirely certain about who attended. I don't recall him being there; that much is certain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. The journalist Sefko Hodzic I think you mentioned was there. Is that your memory, that Hodzic was present?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay -- sorry, go on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: I'm quite certain he was there. He was the one who talked to us. In addition to his own work, he had another objective, which was to publish articles in some of the newspapers. I remember him carrying a camera as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just in relation to the commanders I've listed already, all of those commanders - Gusic, Fazlic, Hakalovic, Sefer Halilovic himself - were all people who were in a position of seniority to Enver Buza. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: I have to say that the Prozor Independent Battalion was an independent unit which had all the powers that an independent unit such as a brigade should have. However, since the other units were larger, and I have the Operations Group West in particular in mind, which I think was composed of two brigades -- well, our commander was in a particular position and I think that his importance in relation to the importance of the commanders of the other units was not as great, naturally. The staff from the corps command and from the General Staff, they were naturally higher up in the military hierarchy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I just -- my question really was this: Did Buza represent to you after the meeting that these people had all come specifically for a meeting with him or did he represent that it was a meeting of a more general kind at which he was just one of the participants?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: You could see that he was only one of the participants; there was nothing else he could have said. But I could not now say exactly what he said in relation to that matter. We all had the impression that he was one of the participants in that meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: And that's that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, after that meeting you were told -- you've indicated you were told certain things by Buza, and your understanding -- sorry, perhaps I should ask you this: You already knew who Sefer Halilovic was from the newspapers and from the press generally. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Sefer Halilovic was a person who had been featured in the -- in the press very, very heavily over the previous year. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And -- in fact, he was a person that those fighting for -- for Bosnia down in the Herzegovina region often used to hope that he would come down and help you out. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes, that's absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And he's become familiar to you as the commander of the army, his official position being Chief of Staff of the Main Staff, but his function being to command the army. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, after he was replaced as the commander of the army by Rasim Delic, there were official communiques from army HQ attempting to explain what changes had been made and, I suggest, also attempting to calm down those soldiers who were very loyal to Sefer Halilovic and who thought very highly of him. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: All I can say is that the official explanations provided in relation to that matter stated that no changes had been made. The General Staff or the staff of the Supreme Command, I don't know what the name was at the time, had simply been fully established and no changes had really been made. That was the official explanation provided.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And certainly they didn't provide you with a list of the new duties of Sefer Halilovic as Chief of Staff as established by a reorganisation order on the 18th of July of 1993. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So what you knew about Sefer's role was what you were told. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: As well as the official information that we had received from the highest level of the military.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And my learned friend the Prosecutor asked you earlier on today whether you ever questioned the authority of Sefer Halilovic or whether you ever heard that authority questioned. And what I want to ask you is this: Was it your job to question the authority of Sefer Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Absolutely not. That wasn't my role nor was that possible at the time. I could not have questioned his authority nor could I have questioned his role within the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You've indicated that you drew a conclusion, or that you were -- you were of the view, of the honest belief, that he was the commander of the operation. What I want to put to you is this: You drew that conclusion because of the information you've just given and because Buza told you that he was here to lead the operation. Is that an accurate summary that I've just put to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: On the whole, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And of course you yourself never asked Sefer Halilovic, nor did he tell you, what his precise function was. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you for that. Now -- I press on now to the next time that Sefer Halilovic came to the -- to the area of the Independent Prozor Battalion. You've indicated, I think, that although you can't recall the precise date, that the Dobro Polje meeting took place on around about the 5th, the 4th, 5th, 6th, somewhere around there. And then you indicated that he came about some days later and you thought approximately six or seven. Is it the fact that Sefer Halilovic came back to Dobro Polje for a visit to Enver Buza on an occasion when you actually were not present yourself but came back later and heard of it? I don't mean the time when he was angry with Buza, I mean on an occasion before that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: I was in Dobro Polje on the first, second, and third time that he came, but I did not attend the meetings. Given the passage of time, I can't say how long it was before he came for the second time. But what I do know is that he might have come for other preparations of the action and for other agreements that they had to reach at the time. This is only something that I can assume, though. I must also inform the Chamber of another fact: The commander of a brigade for whom they said that he was the absolute commander throughout that territory at the time -- well, he was the commander of a brigade who seemed to have such power. That was the situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry. I just missed who you meant on that occasion. Who's the commander of the brigade that you were talking about there? Was that Buza or ...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: I'm referring to all the brigade commanders that had certain stretches of territory under their control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry. Yes. So they appeared to be kings in their own little kingdom. Is that the general effect of what you said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: You could put it that way, but that wasn't the case for the brigades that had been formed of refugees. I'll provide you with an example of one such brigade from Jajce, which was in our territory, and its commander did not really have control of his territory. There were such brigades. There were units from Bosanska Krajina in Travnik, too, units of that kind. But all the brigades that had their own territories, such as our independent battalion, in all those brigades the commanders could allow themselves to behave in this manner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. And I take it, from your observation, that's because the Bosnian army at that time was a relatively immature institution, it was really an army in the process of coming into existence. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let me press on now. The time -- sorry, the chronology that you've given us here is that there was a meeting in Dobro Polje, then six or seven days later there's a second visit by Sefer Halilovic to the Dobro Polje area. Then after that is the occasion that you -- that you noticed the order that you noticed. And then after that again comes the time when Sefer visited for a third time and appeared quite angry with Buza. And I just want to ask you at the moment about that second visit of Sefer's. Now, you've -- you've indicated you didn't attend the meeting. Were you yourself present at the -- at the hut or in the area of the hut at Dobro Polje when Sefer arrived on that second occasion, or were you somewhere else and you came back and found out about that a bit later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: I can't really remember his second visit that well. That is the visit that I have the faintest recollection of. I left that area during that period very briefly. If I did so, it was only for a few hours. If he came during that time, if that's when these things happened, perhaps I was absent then. But I heard from other people who spoke about his arrival in Dobro Polje. I heard a detail from them which can confirm the fact that I remember this very poorly because there was someone, the assistant commander for personnel affairs, who said that he had been with General Halilovic who had assembled a group of combatants. And they had a casual conversation in which they discussed the objectives of the struggle of Bosnia and Herzegovina. But I can't remember that, whereas he claims that this took place for sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. It's just I wanted -- I think you may not be able to comment on this but I'm going to ask you anyway. We've had some evidence from the journalist Hodzic concerning a visit to Dobro Polje that may or may be that occasion. But he indicates that on that occasion Halilovic spoke to the troops, or certain troops, anyway, and indicated that they should behave properly towards civilians and prisoners of war. And I was going to ask you whether you're in a position to confirm that or not, whether Halilovic did make such a speech in the presence of Sefko Hodzic or not. I think I'd still better ask you the question: Can you confirm or deny or say anything about whether that happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: When I spoke to the assistant commander from -- for personal affairs, well, they found out that was the case, but I wasn't there. So -- and this person insisted on the fact that he gave such a speech, that spoke about the objective of establishing a multi-ethnic state. He didn't really speak about the method of fighting for such a state, but -- fighting the civilian population whatever their ethnic -- whatever ethnic group they belonged to was not one of the objectives. This was in fact in Dobro Polje at the time. Perhaps Sefko Hodzic was there at the time; it's quite possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. In any event, from your knowledge, from the media, and I suppose from what other soldiers told you, too, if they talked to you about it, your knowledge was that Sefer Halilovic was a person who was very dedicated to a Bosnian army that would not hurt or slaughter innocent civilians. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Up until September 1993, that's the period we're discussing, the attempts of the ABiH not to destroy the religious buildings of other faiths were emphasised. And they also stated that the population was not persecuted because of the ethnic groups that they belonged to. It was also stated that collection centres were not being established for members of other confessions or ethnic groups. These were objectives that were emphasised and these were the principles that they insisted on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And when you say "they" insisted upon them, Sefer Halilovic, as leader of the army, was one of the leading people who insisted upon that. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly because I had only just met the commander, General Halilovic, at the time. You must understand that the channels of communications were quite poor. But General Halilovic couldn't have had any other positions because if he had had any other positions, he would have had the power to implement them. Given the way the ABiH conducted itself while he was the commander, I think that one can say that they behaved in accordance with the principles I have just referred to. The ABiH conducted itself in a manner in which they showed respect for the principles that I have been referring to. So having provided you with this explanation, I can confirm that that was in fact the case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Well, thank you for that. All right. Now, could I just move now to the occasion at which you looked at the order -- or looked at the -- I take back "order." That you looked at the document in the office of Enver Buza. Now, can I just ask you, you've indicated why it was that you looked at that document, and that was curiosity and concern for what was coming to you and those men you were looking after. Could I just ask you this: In terms of time, how long did you have to look at that document while Commander Buza was out of the room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Perhaps I had a minute or so to examine it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I take it your state of mind at that time was that you, like the others in the battalion, were awaiting orders to go into battle. You knew something was going to happen but you didn't know what so you were awaiting orders. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: That's quite correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And so when you saw this piece of paper sitting on the desk, the immediate inference and conclusion you drew was: This might be the order. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of course you didn't stop to check that document to see whether it was an order or a directive or some other military document; instead, you went straight for the substance of it to see whether it concerned the movements of the Independent Prozor Battalion. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes, in fact that is correct. I didn't have enough time to have a look at the entire document. I just tried to see what the axis of attack of the Prozor Independent Battalion was. And once I had found out what the axis was, I stopped reading the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. So you certainly didn't check the signature on that document to see whether it was Sefer Halilovic or not, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: I have the impression that Sefer Halilovic had signed the document. I can neither confirm whether his name had simply been typed out or whether his name had been typed out and the document also contained signature. For the document to be fully valid, in the lower right-hand corner you should have a typewritten name, his signature, and the stamp of the institution referred to in the upper left-hand corner. Naturally, I didn't have time to check this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the minute that you had, you simply looked to see whether the Independent Prozor Battalion was mentioned; and when you saw that it was, you checked what the details were about its proposed movements and actions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So whether this was an order or a proposal, you are simply unable to comment. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: I couldn't say what it was for certain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. And in fact, at the time no one had explained to you that Sefer Halilovic was, whatever else he may have been, was certainly in charge of an inspection team appointed by Commander Rasim Delic on the 30th of the 8th. At that time no one told you any such thing; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: No one told us anything about that. No one told us that an inspection team had been formed, and no one told us anything about the role of General Delic in the field. I'll repeat this. The only confirmation that we received was that this action would be led by General Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. And because of that information that you had from our Commander Buza, whatever his level of reliability might be, you acted on that information. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS G
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you for that. Now -- very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm now going to move to a topic of showing orders, and in particular I was going to show Witness G the combat report by Commander Buza that refers to that earlier order and then I was going to show him the earlier order and take him through that. It really should all be done at once because of the numbering, which you'll remember. There's a number 1500-27, and doing one tonight and then adjourning for a long time will simply mean that I'll have to do it all again anyway. I apologise for that, but that's the point we've reached.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe we could break here now and we'll continue next Monday. Well, Witness, I'm afraid that you have to spend your weekend in The Hague and you have to understand that now you are under oath during this weekend. So do not let anybody talk to you and do not talk to anybody about your testimony in this courtroom. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand and I do accept that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, thank you very much. And when we adjourn, Madam Usher will pull down the blinds and she will show you out of this courtroom. So you have to stay where you are at this moment. So the hearing is adjourned for this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 11th day of April, 2005, at 2.15 p.m. 24 25
